briefing.text: DATA LAYOUT as reported by the library from the file header (verify on load, do not assume): 158379062.node is an h5ad with 6420 cells x 19918 mouse genes from one sample ('4T1_viable'). obs holds only sample, n_genes and cell_type; there are 11 cell types, 536 cells are labelled 'CAFs', and 49 cells carry a separate 'Pericytes' label (not part of the CAF label). adata.X is dense float32 and appears z-scored and clipped at 10 (a slice had min about -1.9, max exactly 10.0, about 89% negative values), so X is NOT log-normalized. Integer counts are in layers['raw_counts']. var['highly_variable'] (2000 genes) and varm['PCs'] were computed on all 6420 cells. obsm and obsp are empty (no PCA, neighbour graph or UMAP) and there is no adata.raw. uns['log1p'] exists but is an empty dict: do not read its presence as proof that X is log-normalized, and note that some scanpy versions raise KeyError: 'base' in rank_genes_groups because of it; re-running sc.pp.log1p after re-normalizing from raw counts resets it, otherwise set adata.uns['log1p'] = {'base': None}. Do not hide that error with try/except.
briefing.reason: Every later step depends on knowing that X is scaled rather than log-normalized, that raw counts sit in a layer, that no graph exists, and that Pericytes are labelled separately from CAFs; without this the team could cluster or test on the wrong matrix or the wrong cells.

briefing.text: PITFALL: running differential expression on adata.X as delivered. X here is reported to be z-scored and clipped, while scanpy rank_genes_groups expects logarithmized data and computes fold change as expm1(mean_group)/expm1(mean_rest); on scaled values the log fold changes are NaN or meaningless and the t-test/Wilcoxon scores, and therefore the top-50 ranking, differ from the log-normalized result. CHECK: adata.X.min() < 0 and adata.X.max() == 10, and layers['raw_counts'] holds non-negative integers. IF SO: rebuild expression from layers['raw_counts'] (normalize_total then log1p) and run rank_genes_groups on that log-normalized matrix (as X or via layer=), never on the scaled X; keep scaled values only for PCA.
briefing.reason: The deliverable is a ranked gene list; ranking on the scaled matrix instead of log-normalized values changes which genes land in the top 50.

briefing.text: PITFALL: sub-clustering CAFs using the highly variable genes, z-scores and PCs that were computed on the whole dataset (all 11 cell types). Those axes separate fibroblasts from immune/epithelial cells rather than CAF states, so the 6 subclusters become noisy or arbitrary and the membership of the contractile cluster shifts. CHECK: var['highly_variable'] and varm['PCs'] come from all 6420 cells, and X was centred/scaled across all cells (the per-gene mean within the 536 CAFs will not be 0). IF SO: subset to cell_type == 'CAFs' first, re-normalize from layers['raw_counts'], re-select HVGs within the CAF subset, re-scale, re-run PCA and build a new neighbour graph on the subset before Leiden. Do not use sc.tl.leiden(restrict_to=...) on a whole-dataset graph.
briefing.reason: The subclusters define both the target group and the comparison group; clustering on whole-dataset features would change which cells form the contractile cluster and hence the marker list.

briefing.text: PITFALL: Leiden/Louvain has no 'number of clusters' argument; resolution is only a dial, and with about 536 cells the partition (and which cells form the contractile cluster) shifts with resolution, n_neighbors, n_pcs and random seed, sometimes giving a 6-cluster solution with a tiny or unstable cluster. CHECK: scan a resolution grid and record the cluster count, take a resolution giving exactly 6; then repeat over several seeds and 2-3 n_neighbors/n_pcs settings and measure ARI between partitions, the Jaccard overlap of the contractile cluster's cells, and the overlap of its top-50 marker list. IF UNSTABLE: prefer the setting whose contractile cluster is reproducible (near scanpy defaults: n_neighbors about 15, 30-50 PCs or fewer for 536 cells), report the top-50 from that run and state the overlap across runs. Do not hand-merge clusters to reach 6.
briefing.reason: The task fixes the cluster count at 6 but the algorithm does not; how the team reaches exactly 6 and whether the result is stable directly determines the reported gene list.

briefing.text: PITFALL: choosing the 'contractile' subcluster from Acta2 alone or from a UMAP impression. Acta2 is high in more than one CAF state: ECM-producing myofibroblastic CAFs (Postn, Lrrc15, Col11a1, Mmp11, Cthrc1 high) and perivascular/smooth-muscle-like CAFs (Myh11, Rgs5, Mcam, Des, Notch3 high) both express it, and reviews treat 'ECM remodelling' and 'contraction / actin cytoskeleton' as separable programs. CHECK: score all 6 subclusters with a multi-gene contractile/cytoskeletal set in mouse symbols present in var_names (e.g. Acta2, Tagln, Myl9, Mylk, Tpm1, Tpm2, Cnn1, Cnn2, Actg2, Myh11, Des, Cald1, Actn1, Flna, Lmod1) and separately with an ECM set (Col1a1, Col1a2, Col3a1, Postn, Fn1, Lum, Dcn); tabulate cluster mean score and per-gene fraction expressing. IF the top contractile cluster differs from the top ECM cluster, pick the contractile one, because the task asks for contractile/cytoskeletal and not ECM; if two clusters are close, report both scores and choose the one where most individual contractile genes (not a single gene) are highest. A smooth-muscle/pericyte-like cluster inside the CAF label still counts if it has the strongest program, because the task defines CAFs by the given label.
briefing.reason: Picking the wrong subcluster makes the whole top-50 list wrong; this gives a defensible multi-gene rule for the selection and warns about the two states a single marker would confuse.

briefing.text: PITFALL: gene-set scores (scanpy score_genes / Seurat AddModuleScore) can mis-rank clusters. The score subtracts randomly sampled control genes binned by mean expression, so it depends on which matrix is used (clipped z-scores vs log-normalized), on the cell population it is computed in, on the random seed, and it is noisy for short gene lists; signature genes missing from var_names (e.g. human upper-case symbols in a mouse dataset) are dropped, sometimes silently. CHECK: verify every signature gene is in adata.var_names; compute the score on the CAF-only log-normalized matrix; cross-check the cluster ranking with a control-free measure (mean of per-gene z-scores within CAFs, or per-cluster mean log expression of each gene) and with a second seed. IF the methods disagree on the top cluster, trust the control-free per-gene comparison, and afterwards sanity-check that the chosen cluster's DE ranking is consistent with a contractile program.
briefing.reason: The choice of the contractile subcluster rests on a score; if the score is computed on the wrong matrix, with missing genes, or is seed-dependent, the team could select a different cluster.

briefing.text: PITFALL: the wrong background in the marker test. The task asks for the contractile subcluster versus all other CAF subclusters. Running rank_genes_groups on the full object (or with macrophages, epithelial cells etc. in the reference) returns generic fibroblast genes instead of contractile-specific ones. Separately, a pooled 'rest' is dominated by the largest CAF subcluster, so a gene can rank high without being up against every other subcluster. CHECK: the DE object contains exactly the CAF-labelled cells (reported as 536), with groups=[contractile cluster] and reference='rest'; then for the top 50 compute mean log-normalized expression per subcluster and confirm each gene is higher in the contractile cluster than in most or all of the other 5. IF NOT: restrict the test to the CAF subset; keep one-vs-rest as the primary answer (it is what the task states) but flag genes that are only up against the largest subcluster.
briefing.reason: The comparison group defines what counts as a marker; using non-CAF cells as background would replace the requested list with generic fibroblast genes.

briefing.text: PITFALL: restricting the matrix to the 2000 highly variable genes for clustering and then running DE on that same reduced object silently limits the marker list to HVGs, dropping true markers that were not flagged highly variable. CHECK: the object passed to rank_genes_groups has all genes (adata.n_vars, reported as 19918) and log-normalized values, not the HVG-only scaled copy used for PCA. IF NOT: keep two objects or layers, HVG/scaled for PCA and neighbours and full-gene log-normalized for scoring and DE, and transfer only the cluster labels between them.
briefing.reason: A top-50 list drawn from only 2000 genes can miss real markers; this is a silent error that would not raise any warning.

briefing.text: PITFALL: 'top 50 markers' depends on how genes are ranked. Scanpy ranks by the test score (z-statistic), Seurat by p-value then fold change; ranking by log fold change alone selects very lowly expressed genes with huge unstable logFC; ranking by p-value gives ties at 0; rankby_abs=True lets down-regulated genes into the list; scanpy Wilcoxon has tie_correct=False by default although sparse counts are heavily tied; p-values are inflated anyway because the clusters were defined from the same data, and with one sample no pseudobulk is possible. CHECK: with pts=True confirm all 50 genes have positive score and positive logFC and are expressed in a reasonable fraction of the contractile cluster (e.g. >=10-25%), and compare the top-50 from Wilcoxon (tie_correct=True) with the t-test top-50. IF they differ: use up-regulated genes only, ranked by Wilcoxon score on log-normalized data (benchmarks support Wilcoxon, t-test and logistic regression as the best performers), not by logFC or raw p-value, and report the overlap between methods rather than treating p-values as evidence.
briefing.reason: The answer is exactly a ranked top-50; the ranking statistic and direction filter decide list membership, so the team needs an explicit, defensible ranking rule.

briefing.text: PITFALL: when one annotated cell type is re-clustered, some subclusters are artifacts rather than states: heterotypic doublets or mislabelled cells (most cells in this dataset are myeloid, so CAF+macrophage doublets with Ptprc/Lyz2/C1qa, or epithelial carry-over with Epcam/Krt8/Krt18), a cycling cluster (Mki67, Top2a), or low-quality cells with few genes. Such a cluster uses up one of the 6 slots and sits in the 'rest' group, changing both the partition and the fold changes. CHECK: per subcluster, tabulate mean expression of Ptprc, Lyz2, Epcam, Krt18, Pecam1, Mki67, Top2a and the distribution of obs['n_genes'] and total counts. IF FOUND: make sure the cluster picked as contractile is not such an artifact and that its top-50 is not led by immune/epithelial/cell-cycle genes; keep all CAF-labelled cells as the primary analysis (the task defines CAFs by the provided label) and, as a sensitivity check only, repeat with the artifact cluster removed and report how much the top-50 changes.
briefing.reason: An artifact subcluster can be mistaken for a state or distort the 'rest' background; the check is cheap and tells the team whether the selected cluster and its markers are trustworthy without changing the task's definition of CAFs.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team's 6-cluster partition contains a small cluster whose own top markers are hypoxia/glycolysis genes plus an epithelial keratin, and on a broad contractile/cytoskeletal score that small cluster was nearly tied with a much larger cluster carrying the classic smooth-muscle actin/myosin genes. Your records list a doublet-like cluster and a cycling cluster but no hypoxic one. Check whether such hypoxic or keratin-positive cells exist among your 536 CAFs, which of your six clusters they fall in, and in particular whether they sit inside your chosen contractile cluster or in the rest group. Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: both teams scanned Leiden resolution for the first value giving exactly 6 clusters on what reads as the same pipeline, yet the two teams stopped at different resolutions and the resulting clusters do not have the same sizes. Check which unstated details decide your partition: the HVG flavor and whether a batch key or a max_value clip was used, the PCA solver and seed, the resolution grid start and step, and the Leiden implementation and its iteration setting. Then check whether your contractile cluster keeps the same cells across every resolution in your grid that yields 6 clusters, not only the first. Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: you ran the Wilcoxon test with tie correction switched on and kept up-regulated genes only; the other team recorded a plain Wilcoxon call ranked by score with no non-default options noted. You also recorded that the top list moves noticeably between tests. Check how many of your top 50 change, and how their order changes, between your call and the toolkit's plain default call on the same clusters. What in the task text or the data supports a non-default setting over the default one? Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your plan listed a robustness check of the chosen cluster across resolutions and seeds, and your notes say it was not run. The other team ran it and found that the 6-cluster partition is reproducible across seeds and most graph settings, but that one setting with fewer neighbours and fewer PCs gave a contractile cluster with almost no cells in common with its primary one. Check, in your data, the cell overlap of your chosen cluster and the overlap of its top-50 list across several seeds, two or three neighbour/PC settings, and every resolution in your grid that yields 6 clusters. Record which HVG flavor, PCA solver, seed and Leiden implementation you used. Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your plan said to pick the top-scoring cluster, your score came out nearly tied, and you then chose by judgement rather than by the score. Your gene set included ubiquitous cytoskeletal genes (Actb, Vim and others). The other team scored a narrower set limited to smooth-muscle actin, myosin light chain, calponin, tropomyosin and related genes, used a control-free per-gene z-score as well as score_genes with more than one seed, and counted how many individual set genes are highest in each cluster; it saw several actin-high clusters with close scores, one of them cycling. Check whether your near-tie persists when the ubiquitous genes are left out, when the score is computed without random control genes or with other seeds, and when you count per-gene winners; check also whether a cluster of that small size gives a stable mean. State the selection rule you would have written before seeing the scores. Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team recorded the exact settings of its marker test: all genes rather than HVGs only, log-normalised values, up-regulated genes only, tie correction on; it also found that the top list changes noticeably between a Wilcoxon test and a t-test, and it re-ran the test with the macrophage-like doublet cluster removed from the rest group. Your notes say only 'Wilcoxon, top 50 by score'. Check which of these settings your call actually used (tie correction, gene universe, whether any gene in your 50 has a negative score or fold change), and how many of your top 50 survive each variation, including leaving out the macrophage-like cluster and the small hypoxic cluster from the rest group. Does that change your method?

referee.difference: Same pipeline (536 CAFs, renormalised, 2000 HVG, 30 PC, 15 NN, Leiden 6 clusters, plain Wilcoxon vs rest). They differ only in the contractile cluster's boundary. X's cluster has 112 cells; Y's has 126 cells: the same 112 plus 14 border cells. Both partitions reproduce: igraph res 0.46-0.50 gives 112 cells (50/50 genes match X), res 0.44/0.52/0.54 gives 126 cells (50/50 match Y). 42/50 genes are shared.
referee.test: test3.py: I split the cells into core112, extra14 and rest. For each group I computed the mean per-gene z-score of a smooth-muscle/contractile set, a hypoxia set (Ndrg1, Bnip3, Egln3, Slc2a1, Ca9, Pgk1, Vegfa, Ldha), and each candidate's 8 unique genes.
referee.expected_if_x: The extra14 cells are less contractile than the core and carry a separate (e.g. hypoxic) program, so adding them dilutes the contractile cluster. Y's unique genes would then come from the extra14 cells.
referee.expected_if_y: The extra14 cells are as contractile as the core and not set apart by another program, so they belong to the cluster.
referee.outcome: Smooth-muscle z-score: core 0.47, extra14 0.13, rest -0.13. Hypoxia z-score: core 0.08, extra14 1.29, rest -0.07. Y's unique genes (Gapdh, Pkm, Cd63, Timp1...): extra14 0.94 vs core 0.47. X's unique genes (Tpm1, Cnn3, Col1a1...): core 0.56 vs extra14 -0.08. In the 112-cell partition the extra14 cells join the hypoxic cluster 2.
referee.reason: The 14 cells that only Y includes are hypoxic and weakly contractile. They bring glycolytic/hypoxia genes into Y's top 50 and push out contractile/cytoskeletal genes such as Tpm1 and Cnn3. X's 112-cell cluster is the purer contractile subcluster. Caveat: the 126-cell partition appears at more resolutions, so the boundary itself is a setting choice, but on contractile purity the data favour X.

questions.question: In scanpy, what are the defaults of sc.tl.leiden (flavor/backend leidenalg versus igraph, n_iterations, random_state, directed) in recent versions, and can the two backends or iteration settings return different partitions and different cluster counts at the same resolution on a graph of a few hundred cells?
questions.why: Both teams scanned for 'the first resolution giving 6 clusters' on nominally the same pipeline and stopped at different resolutions with different cluster sizes; knowing what the default call does tells them which partition a plain standard run would produce.

questions.question: In scanpy's rank_genes_groups with method='wilcoxon', how is the reported score computed, what is the default of tie_correct, and does switching tie_correct on change the order of top-ranked genes (not just the p-values) for sparse log-normalised single-cell data? Which settings does a plain default call use for ranking 'top N markers'?
questions.why: One team used tie correction and the other recorded a plain call; if tie correction reorders genes near rank 50, it explains part of the disagreement and tells the teams which call a standard pipeline corresponds to.

questions.question: In published classifications of cancer-associated fibroblast subtypes in mouse tumours, which genes define a contractile / actin-cytoskeleton (myofibroblast or vascular smooth-muscle-like) CAF program as distinct from an ECM-producing myofibroblastic program and from a hypoxia- or glycolysis-associated CAF state, and do such signatures include ubiquitous cytoskeletal genes such as Actb or Vim?
questions.why: The teams scored 'contractile/cytoskeletal' with gene sets of different breadth, and with the broad set a small hypoxic cluster nearly tied; a reference definition of the program would settle which gene set and therefore which cluster the phrase points to.

findings.question: In scanpy, what are the defaults of sc.tl.leiden (flavor/backend leidenalg versus igraph, n_iterations, random_state, directed) in recent versions, and can the two backends or iteration settings return different partitions and different cluster counts at the same resolution on a graph of a few hundred cells?
findings.answer: Defaults: resolution=1, random_state=0, n_iterations=-1 (run to convergence), directed=None, flavor=None, partition_type=RBConfigurationVertexPartition. flavor=None currently runs leidenalg on a directed graph and raises a FutureWarning saying the default will move to flavor='igraph', n_iterations=2, directed=False, and that 'results will be slightly different with the changed backend'. scanpy's own tests only require NMI > 0.9 between the leidenalg and igraph outputs, not identical labels, and they assert that different seeds give different partitions. So backend, n_iterations, directed or seed can change cluster membership. Near the resolution where the count moves from 5 to 6 to 7 they can also change the cluster count. A plain sc.tl.leiden(adata, resolution=r) uses leidenalg, directed, n_iterations=-1 and seed 0. The teams should record these settings and scan resolution with one fixed call.

findings.question: In scanpy's rank_genes_groups with method='wilcoxon', how is the reported score computed, what is the default of tie_correct, and does switching tie_correct on change the order of top-ranked genes (not just the p-values) for sparse log-normalised single-cell data? Which settings does a plain default call use for ranking 'top N markers'?
findings.answer: The score is the rank-sum z-statistic: z = (R_group - n1(n1+n2+1)/2) / sqrt(tc * n1*n2*(n1+n2+1)/12). The default is tie_correct=False, which sets tc=1. With tie_correct=True, tc = 1 - sum(t^3 - t)/(N^3 - N), computed per gene. Genes are ordered by score. Because tc differs between genes, tie correction scales each z by its own factor 1/sqrt(tc_gene), and genes with many zeros (ties) get the largest boost. So it can reorder genes, especially in the lower part of a top-50 list, not only change p-values. This is inferred from the formula; I found no published measurement of the size of the effect. Defaults of a plain call: method=None, which means t-test, not wilcoxon; reference='rest'; rankby_abs=False; tie_correct=False; corr_method='benjamini-hochberg'. A standard Wilcoxon call is therefore rank_genes_groups(..., method='wilcoxon') with tie_correct=False.
findings.confidence: high for the defaults and formula; medium that reordering is material near rank 50 (inferred, not measured)

findings.question: In published classifications of cancer-associated fibroblast subtypes in mouse tumours, which genes define a contractile / actin-cytoskeleton (myofibroblast or vascular smooth-muscle-like) CAF program as distinct from an ECM-producing myofibroblastic program and from a hypoxia- or glycolysis-associated CAF state, and do such signatures include ubiquitous cytoskeletal genes such as Actb or Vim?
findings.answer: Contractile, vascular or smooth-muscle-like CAFs are defined by smooth-muscle contractile genes. Examples: Cords 2023 vCAF (ACTA2, MCAM, RGS5); pan-myCAF in Clin Cancer Res 2021 (ACTA2, MYH11, MCAM, TAGLN, MYLK; GO term smooth muscle contraction); colorectal CAF-B (ACTA2, TAGLN, PDGFA, MUSTN1, NOTCH3, MYH11); Bartoschek 2018 mouse vCAF (perivascular, Notch3/Kcnj8). ECM or matrix CAFs are defined by MMP11, CDH11, POSTN, collagens (COL1A2, COL11A1, COL10A1, COL12A1) and COMP; the mouse mCAF set is Fbln1, Pdgfra, Dcn, Vcan, Col14a1, Cxcl14. The hypoxic or glycolytic 'tumour-like' CAF (Cords tCAF) is defined by PDPN, MME, ENO1, NDRG1 and CA9. None of these signatures includes Actb or Vim. A narrow smooth-muscle set (Acta2, Tagln, Myh11, Mylk, Myl9, Cnn1, Des, Mcam, Rgs5, Notch3) matches the references; broad sets that include Actb or Vim do not, and they can let a hypoxic cluster tie. Caveat: the gateway cut off the page texts before the results sections, so the Cords Table 1 and Clin Cancer Res marker lists come from search excerpts, and most of the reference signatures are human with mouse symbols mapped.
